text:
"Monitor Claude Code" could mean a couple of different things — here's the breakdown:

**1. Watch a live process during a session (most likely what you want)**
Claude has a `Monitor` tool: it starts a shell command that runs for the session and streams every stdout line back as a notification (e.g. `tail -F build.log`, polling a deploy status). It's fire-and-forget input only — it can't block or take action, just report. You can ask me directly, e.g. "monitor the dev server logs and tell me if it crashes," and I'll arm it via that tool. It auto-stops after a timeout (default 5 min) unless you ask for `persistent: true`, and you can cancel it any time.

**2. Auto-start a watcher every session (via a plugin)**
If you want something that watches a log/file/service automatically every time you start Claude Code (not just when you ask), that's the plugin `monitors/monitors.json` component — same underlying mechanism, but declared in a plugin instead of requested ad hoc. It's still experimental, pure-input (no blocking), and has some sharp edges (e.g. it dies with the session, doesn't survive `/reload-plugins` after a plugin update, and won't load at all from a project-scope skills plugin).

**3. Observability of Claude Code's own usage** (cost, tokens, tool calls across your team)
That's a different thing entirely — OpenTelemetry metrics/logs export, not covered by the mechanisms above. Let me know if that's actually what you're after and I can look into it separately.

Which of these did you have in mind — watching a specific process/log right now, setting up an always-on plugin watcher, or usage/cost telemetry?
